multipleChoice.question: Which concern frames the discussion of acne?
options: How teenagers choose among competing skin products.
How visible skin problems can affect a person's life.
Why doctors classify several kinds of skin condition.
Why most skin conditions disappear after adolescence.

multipleChoice.question: How is the range of acne described?
options: It is limited to marks on the face and neck.
It progresses from mild cases to cysts in everyone.
It is mainly a condition that begins in adulthood.
It includes less severe spots and more serious forms.

multipleChoice.question: Which group does the doctor identify as the largest among her acne patients?
options: People in their teenage years.
Women in their forties.
Children before puberty.
Adults of every age equally.

multipleChoice.question: An adult dismisses a teenager's mild acne because it is not medically severe. Which response best follows from the doctor's account?
options: Mild acne always develops into a more serious form.
Mild acne can stop puberty from progressing normally.
Mild acne can still seriously affect social relationships.
Mild acne usually needs treatment through adulthood.

multipleChoice.question: How does the explanation of acne's causes challenge a possible social judgement?
options: It presents acne as linked to inherited and natural processes.
It presents acne as a result of poor personal choices.
It presents acne as a response to pressure from friends.
It presents acne as a problem created by treatment.

multipleChoice.question: What can be inferred about the doctor's earlier attempts to manage her acne?
options: She rejected specialist treatment after trying it.
She received prescriptions through her family doctor.
She tried shop-bought options because specialist care was unaffordable.
She waited until adulthood before trying any treatment.

multipleChoice.question: Why does the doctor mention having tried treatments she recommends?
options: To show that every patient will respond in the same way.
To suggest that professional training is unnecessary.
To explain why she stopped using other treatments.
To show that her advice also draws on lived experience.

multipleChoice.question: Which broader message follows from the doctor's later work and the explanation of acne's causes?
options: Personal difficulties prevent people from supporting others.
A natural condition can be faced with informed support.
Acne should always be managed without professional advice.
Everyone's acne ends at the same stage of adulthood.
